title: How a missed parking payment ended in a credit for a Port tenant

beats.text: One cruise operator paid San Francisco rent under two waterfront leases.

visual.sub: One tenant had two rent formulas and missing cash records

beats.text: From 2009 through 2011, Hornblower paid the Port more than five million dollars.

visual.kicker: One tenant had two rent formulas and missing cash records

beats.text: At Pier 3, a missed parking entry meant $7,578 in rent was due.

visual.label: At Pier 3, one parking month produced a rent shortfall

beats.text: Hornblower acknowledged the calculation error and disputed the Port’s reading of the lease.

visual.kicker: At Pier 3, one parking month produced a rent shortfall

beats.text: Employee service charges pushed the numbers the other way.

visual.line: A lease exclusion for employee payments

beats.text: The lease exclusion gave Hornblower a $28,816 credit.

visual.label: Employee service charges produced a larger credit at the same pier

beats.text: Overpayments on the second lease added a $7,216 credit.

visual.kicker: The second lease had offsetting errors of its own

beats.text: After late fees, the audit put the net overpayment at $25,599.

visual.label: The second lease had offsetting errors of its own

beats.text: It credited the tenant $36,032. All twelve recommendations closed.

visual.label: The Port reported collection and credited the tenant

beats.text: Every source is linked in the case file below.
